title: RxnOptBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Reaction-Condition Optimization in Organic Methodology
claim: A benchmark builds questions from real screening tables in paired evidence modes and scores them with precomputed continuous relative scores.
layout: 2 panels (A left, B right), top-to-bottom flows, annotated table plus score formula
description: A two-part figure on a wide canvas. Part A (left, blue header) shows a reaction scheme and a condition-screening table with 18 rows. The table is split into 'reagent sweep' (yellow highlight) and 'solvent sweep' (teal highlight). A pink dashed row marks the top result that is 'never leak', and purple rows are 'picked as precedents'. Below the table, two dashed boxes compare 'With Precedents Mode' and 'Without Precedents Mode'. Each box shows a question, options, the input, and the output. Part B (right, orange header) has three steps. Step 1 gives the effective-score formula with a worked example and arrows. Step 2 covers multiple choice, with a bar chart and the Acc and Score metrics. Step 3 covers fill-in-blank, with bars, Hit, Acc and Score metrics, and a table of four predictions. Pastel colors and a pink 'best' highlight guide the eye.
caption: RxnOptBench overview. (A) Question Construction: each condition-screening table yields MC/FIB items in matched precedents (prior rows shown, top withheld) and no-precedents (no prior rows) modes. (B) Scoring Rules: every observed row carries a precomputed relative score fusing yield with ee/dr/rr. MC reports Accuracy and Score; FIB separately reports observed-row Hit, Strict Accuracy, and Score conditioned on Hit.
abstract: Chemical reaction-condition optimization -- choosing the catalyst, ligand, solvent, reagent, temperature, time, and atmosphere that jointly maximize yield and stereoselectivity -- is a central, judgement-laden subtask of organic methodology research that large language models are increasingly expected to support. Yet existing chemistry benchmarks evaluate reaction-class labelling, retrosynthesis, or SMILES manipulation, and do not ask models to read a real condition-screening table and pick the best set. We introduce RxnOptBench, a benchmark whose every option and precedent is a real wet-lab entry mined from the optimization tables of organic-methodology papers published in 2025, graded by a continuous relative score derived from a declared headline utility that combines reported yield with enantiomeric excess (ee), diastereomeric ratio (dr), and regioisomeric ratio (rr), and equipped with a paired precedents-vs-no-precedents design that isolates in-context use of literature evidence from parametric memorization. Across nine frontier LLMs and three Chemistry LLMs, even the best models leave substantial headroom: chemistry-specialized models fall to the random-baseline floor on multi-axis selection, while open-weight models have closed most of the gap to proprietary frontier models. We release the final human-reviewed benchmark test set and evaluation code.
